theron04.title: The Delivery
theron04.d01: Night at the port. The pilgrim from Corinth prays alone on the quay, a bronze key tied to her belt.
theron04.t_escriba: At the end of the quay, the scribe from the market shows his tablet to two guards. He remembers the trick and forgets the trickster. I never thought that could save me and insult me at the same time.
theron04.d_rival: He didn't take the job, but he came anyway. Across the quay, a hooded man is waiting for her too. The other one the patrician sent. A less gentle one.
theron04.c_rival: The hooded man starts walking toward the pilgrim.
theron04.c_rival.first: Get to her before he does.
theron04.c_rival.watch: Let it happen. Not your problem.
theron04.d_first: He crosses the quay faster than the hood. No one notices a man no one remembers. The other hesitates, misses his moment and slips back into the shadow.
theron04.d_watch: The hood reaches her. A shove, a short cry, and the pilgrim's belt is empty. No one on the quay remembers seeing anything.
theron04.t_watch: Not my problem. Then why am I heading for the tunnel too?
theron04.t_livia: Last night a priestess crossed this quay with temple fire in her hands, and she looked at me. Really looked. Two people in one week. The threads are tightening around something.
theron04.d02: Hestia, keep the house I no longer have. Keep my son, wherever he is.
theron04.e01.hint: The key is on her belt. Look around (E) and get close.
theron04.h.belt.1: A belt of braided wool. The key sits on the inside, tied by a cord with three turns of a knot. A mother's knot: firm, made by someone who has lost things before.
theron04.h.net.1: Nets drying on the quay. Some were mended by hands he knows. The mending has Nerea's stitch.
theron04.d03: Are you looking for someone too? You have the face of someone who's lost.
theron04.d03_helped: You. The man with the silver. Dion slept without fever his last night. His last. I wanted someone to know he slept well.
theron04.d03_conned: I know those hands. The cup hands. Stay away from my belt.
theron04.gh: what ties the pilgrim to that key?
theron04.c01: The key is a hand's breadth from his fingers.
theron04.c01.steal: Distract her and undo the knot at her belt.
theron04.c01.ask: Tell her the truth and ask for the key.
theron04.msteal.hint: Talk to her, and undo one turn of the knot each time she looks at the sea.
theron04.msteal.hint_wary: She distrusts your hands. Undo the knot only when she looks at the sea.
theron04.msteal.clean: Took the key without her noticing.
theron04.msteal.sloppy: Took the key, but she suspected.
theron04.msteal.caught: She caught him with his hand on her belt.
theron04.d_stolen: The key passes from her belt to his sleeve, light as a coin. She goes on praying for a house she no longer has.
theron04.d_sloppy: Wait... Did you touch my belt? ...No. It can't have been. I don't even know who you are.
theron04.d_caught: She grabs his wrist. He pulls. The cord snaps, and the key ends up in the wrong hand. Her scream follows him all the way to the tunnel.
theron04.t_caught: Tomorrow she won't remember my face. Only the hand.
theron04.d_ask: A patrician wants what lies under the Temple? ...Take it. If a house key opens a door for someone, let it. But come back with it.
theron04.d_ask2: She gives him the key and holds his hand a moment longer. For the first time in years, someone looks him in the eye while he barely lies.
theron04.t_bound: Too many people are holding my threads this week. My hand won't cut anyone's grief tonight. Nor their hope.
theron04.mgrief.hint: The threads that hold the pilgrim. Cut, loosen or tie.
theron04.mgrief.hint_bound: The threads that hold the pilgrim. His hand cannot cut her grief or her hope.
theron04.mgrief.cut_chave: Cut the thread between the pilgrim and the key.
theron04.mgrief.loosen_chave: Loosened the thread of the key.
theron04.d_cut_chave: This key? Keep it. It's only bronze. I don't know why I carry it.
theron04.d_loosen_chave: A house where no one lives doesn't need a key, does it? Take it. Maybe it opens something better.
theron04.d_cut_luto: Son? I have no son. I came to Aurelia... for what, again? The key? Take it. It's heavy.
theron04.d_loosen_luto: He went to sea. It's all right to cry for him a little less tonight. Here, take the key. I'll come back tomorrow.
theron04.d_cut_esperanca: He won't come back. None of them come back. Take the key, open whatever you like. It doesn't matter anymore.
theron04.d_loosen_esperanca: Maybe he won't come back. Maybe. ...But the key stays with me.
theron04.d_tie: As long as I cry for him, he's alive somewhere. Take the key. I'll wait here, crying and waiting.
theron04.d_none: He lowers his hand. The pilgrim's threads stay as they are: pain and hope, all tied to the same key.
theron04.d_price: ...Sir? Are you all right? Were you talking to me? Sorry, my mind wandered.
theron04.t_price: She doesn't even know she gave me anything. And I no longer quite know what I took.
theron04.d_nokey: With no key, he waits for the hooded man to open the shrine door. He slips in behind him, like a shadow. The hood never looks back.
theron04.d_tunnel: The tunnel of waves. The walls are painted with sea, and real water beats on the other side of the stone. The urn grows heavier with every step.
theron04.etunnelguard.hint: The guard dozes on his feet, leaning on his spear. Walk past him slowly (hold Shift) and he won't wake.
theron04.d_quinto: Halt! Who... Oh. You again? No. I've never seen you. Why did I say "again"?
theron04.d_quinto2: No one ever sees me twice, guard. Go do your round.
theron04.t_quinto: Even the guards learn to forget me on their own.
theron04.etunnel.hint: Follow the tunnel to the end.
theron04.h.waves.1: The waves painted on the wall are lines of thread. He looks closer: they are real threads, fixed in the stone, all running the same way. Down.
theron04.d_portals: The chamber of the three portals. The closed eye, the waves, the smooth stone. The air smells of burnt thread, like the urn.
theron04.d_trace: On the floor, traces of someone who came before: lamp wax and the prints of huge hands on the wall. He is not alone beneath the city.
theron04.d_asterion: Something breathes in the dark, behind the portal of smooth stone. Big. Very big. Its threads are thick as ship's rope, and one of them shines like his: a thread no one remembers.
theron04.d_asterion2: He lays his hand on the bronze of the closed-eye portal. On the other side, the breathing stops.
theron04.d_refused_end: The urn isn't with him. Further on, he hears the hood set something heavy down before the portal of the eye. The patrician will have what he wanted, with or without him.
theron04.t_urn: The remains of an old mistake, the patrician said. No one pays that much to bury a mistake. They pay to wake it.
theron04.t_urn_up: Caio's threads rise to the ceiling. This urn isn't for him. It's for whoever holds the other end.
theron04.t_urn.second: A hero would carry it back, whatever it cost. But heroes are remembered. I'm only the man who carries.
theron04.c_urn: Before the portal of the eye, the urn waits to be left.
theron04.c_urn.break: Break the urn and scatter what's inside.
theron04.c_urn.return: Take the urn and the key back to the pilgrim.
theron04.d_deliver: The urn stays before the portal. The wax melts by itself. Somewhere in the Temple, far above, a flame goes out.
theron04.d_break: The lead cracks and the ashes rise like burnt threads. For a moment, every thread in the chamber tangles. Then, silence. The patrician will know.
theron04.d_return: He carries the urn back. It's heavier going back. It's always heavier going back. The patrician will know.
theron04.d_fled: In the market, Nerea's spot is empty, swept clean. A boy hands him a piece of net with a carefully tied knot: "The woman said you'd understand."
theron04.t_fled: She left because I asked. She's alive somewhere, mending other people's nets. And she still owes me a fish.
theron04.d_men: At the other end of the street, College men. A scribe reads names from a tablet. They head straight for the mending stall.
theron04.c_last: Nerea doesn't look up from her needle. She has already seen the men.
theron04.c_last.shout: Shout his own name, so they look at him, not at her.
theron04.c_last.shadow: Stay in the shadow. No one sees a man no one remembers.
theron04.d_shout: THÉRON! The man you're looking for is here!
theron04.d_shout2: The men turn to him. For a moment, they remember. He sees the name light up in each pair of eyes and go out right after.
theron04.d_alive_after: The College men leave without knowing why they came. At the stall, the needle never stopped once.
theron04.d_taken_now: The College men take Nerea by the arm. She doesn't resist. She folds the net before she stands, like someone who means to come back.
theron04.d_taken_words: Mend it yourself, Théron. Yours, at least.
theron04.d_taken: In the market, Nerea's patchwork blanket lies on the ground, empty. The needle is stuck in the net, in the middle of a stitch.
theron04.t_taken: The College took the only person who said my name. She isn't dead. I know because I don't remember forgetting her.
theron04.d_dead1: The College men reach the stall. No one shouts. No one in the market looks.
theron04.d_dead2: Théron. I knew you'd come. Sit. I haven't finished yours yet.
theron04.d_dead3: Afterwards, no one at the port remembers seeing the College men. Only the unfinished net, with a name sewn into the stitch.
theron04.t_dead: She sewed my name. Who will remember it now?
theron04.d_warned: The men in white came back today. They asked, they wrote, they left. They didn't find what they wanted. Yet.
theron04.d_alive1: In the market, Nerea mends nets by lamplight, as if the whole night had been just a night.
theron04.d_alive2: Théron. You came back with lighter hands. Or heavier. Sit here and I'll see.
theron04.t_alive: She still remembers. For now, that's enough.
theron04.d02_missed: They said a priestess came looking for me last night, here on the quay, with fire in her hands. I was with my son. I came too late.
theron04.d02_broken: A priestess promised me an ember from her flame. I waited all night. She never came.
theron04.d_trace_empty: On the floor, only dust and old prints of huge hands on the wall. Something lives down here. Tonight, it isn't home.
theron04.c_tunnel: A young guard dozes on his feet in the middle of the tunnel, leaning on his spear.
theron04.c_tunnel.sneak: Slip past him slowly, without waking him.
theron04.c_tunnel.bribe: Wake him with the silver from the path in hand.
theron04.d_bribe: Silver? I didn't see anything. I never see anything. ...Why does everyone pay me not to see you?
theron04.d_taken_shout: One of them blinks, confused, and goes back to his tablet. Nerea's name is still there, written before he shouted.
theron04.d_cause_intro: Nerea, the net woman. By order of the College. Reasons:
theron04.d_cause_colegio_procura_theron: "...says out loud a name scraped from the book of vows. A Vestal read that name at the Night Rite, before the augur."
theron04.d_cause_caio: "...denounced by a patrician, Caius Licinius: she knows the man who broke a contract with him."
theron04.d_cause_ameaca: "...named by a patrician as an acquaintance of a man he hired."
theron04.d_cause_alerta: "...tonight's general order: knocking under the Temple, a monster in the galleries, swindles at the port. Take whoever knows names."
theron04.d_cause_ignorada: "...was warned we were asking for her. She did not move."
theron04.d_lie_exposed: "...and denied knowing him, though she said his name at the market, before witnesses. Lying to the College is a fault too."
theron04.d_wait: Somewhere on the quay, a woman from Corinth waits for a key he promised to bring back. It will not come back.
theron04.t_livia_named: Yesterday a priestess said my name on this quay. Out loud. The stone didn't swallow it, the water didn't take it. It's still in the air.
theron04.t_livia_named.second: Whoever says your name ties you to the world. Remember what that cost last time.
theron04.t_livia_ember: Her lamp is still warm at my belt. Temple fire, trusted to a man no one remembers. She didn't even ask if I was a thief.
theron04.d02_kept: She came, the priestess. She waited with me until the bell, and Díon could go. Tonight I pray for her, not for him.
theron04.c_ember: The priestess's lamp weighs at his belt. The ember still lives.
theron04.c_ember.give: Hand over the lamp: "The priestess kept her word."
theron04.c_ember.keep: Keep it. Temple fire is worth silver in the right market.
theron04.d_ember: Fire from her flame... She sent it. She didn't forget.
theron04.d_ember2: Iante lights a wick from the ember. For a moment, in the water's reflection, a boy raises his hand. She looks at Théron like someone she will remember.
theron04.t_ast1.man: footsteps. no. there are no footsteps. but the air on the other side moved.
theron04.e_ast.hint: There is no sound at all beyond the bronze. F sniffs. Go to the gate.
theron04.t_ast2.man: a ghost? ghosts have no smell. this one does: salt, wax, burnt thread.
theron04.t_ast2.beast: no sound. hunter. kill before it kills.
theron04.c_door: On the other side of the bronze, an enormous hand presses too. The warmth comes through the metal.
theron04.gh_ast: what thread ties this thing to the world?
theron04.c_door.tell: Confess to the bronze: "I'm the one who opened your gate. I cut the keeper's thread."
theron04.c_door.alive: Say what the thread showed: "The boy is alive."
theron04.c_door.sorry: Say what the thread showed: "I'm sorry about the boy."
theron04.c_door.silent: Take his hand off the bronze and go on with the urn. Whatever lives here is not his problem.
theron04.d_g_ast: The thing's threads pass through the bronze, thick as ship's ropes. One of them was cut and tied again, like his. Another, thin, rises toward the city.
theron04.d_g_dead: The thin thread ends in a cut tip. It belonged to a boy. The thing still holds it, the way one holds a hand that is no longer there.
theron04.d_g_with: The thin thread doesn't rise: it loops back and ties to the thick one, down here. The boy is on the far side, with it. Alive.
theron04.d_g_alive: The thin thread belongs to a boy, and it still beats, up in the city. The thing holds it like the last rope of a boat.
theron04.d_tell: Silence. Then, from the other side, one knock on the bronze. Just one. It isn't a threat. It's the knock of someone answering.
theron04.d_alive: The breathing on the other side breaks, like a sob too big. Then one knock on the bronze. Just one.
theron04.d_sorry: Nothing, for a long time. Then one slow knock, and the hand on the other side stays on the bronze until he walks away.
theron04.d_silent: He takes his hand away. On the other side, the thing sniffs the place where he stood, long after he is gone.
